answer.decision: Choose tail-aware sampling that retains all error traces and p99-or-slower traces while keeping a lower random sample of normal successful traffic.
answer.action: Roll out the validated post-assembly tail-sampling policy gradually. Retain 100% of errors and p99-or-slower requests, tune normal-traffic sampling to preserve at least a 40% cost reduction, and monitor retention by service and route to protect latency-analysis coverage.
reasons: The prototype reduced stored trace volume by 55%, exceeding the required 40% reduction.
The prototype retained all injected error and p99 test traces, satisfying the rare-error and very-slow-request goals.
Error traces are disproportionately useful: 0.7% of requests account for 46% of traces used in incident reviews.
Normal successful traffic exceeds 98% of volume, making it the appropriate target for reduced retention.
Independent fully aggregated metrics preserve broad service-level latency measurement, while sampled traces support detailed investigation.
The backend supports retention decisions after span assembly, so the policy is technically feasible.
assumptions: Stored trace volume is a sufficiently accurate proxy for telemetry cost.
The prototype traffic and injected tests are representative enough for a controlled rollout.
The p99 threshold is the intended definition of a very slow request.
Normal-trace sampling can be monitored or stratified by service and route to maintain useful coverage.
risks: Tail sampling adds buffering, processing latency, and sampler-capacity requirements.
Low-volume services or routes may be undersampled if one global random rate is used.
Incorrect error classification or latency thresholds could discard valuable traces.
Production traffic may differ from the prototype and require adjustment to achieve the cost target without harming analysis.

citations.claim: The prototype reduced stored trace volume by 55% while retaining all injected error and p99 test traces.
Errors represent 0.7% of requests but account for 46% of traces used during incident reviews.
Requests above the p99 latency threshold represent 1% of volume.
Normal successful traffic represents more than 98% of trace volume.
Metrics are independently collected at full aggregation and do not require every trace to be retained.
The backend supports tail-based retention decisions after spans are assembled.
